## Q1
What is the maximum Hamming distance among all pairs of the following binary codes?

| Code | Binary value |
|---|---|
| C₁ | 00000 |
| C₂ | 01011 |
| C₃ | 10101 |

## Q1 - Options
(A) 2
(B) 3
(C) 4
(D) 5

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Hamming Code, Error Detection & Bit Stuffing
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q27

C₁ and C₂ differ in three positions, C₁ and C₃ differ in three positions, while C₂ = 01011 and C₃ = 10101 differ in four positions. Thus the maximum pairwise Hamming distance is 4.

## Q4
What is the minimum Hamming Distance in a block code if we want to be able to detect up to S errors?

## Q4 - Options
(A) S
(B) S+1
(C) 1
(D) 0

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Hamming Code, Error Detection & Bit Stuffing
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q35

To reliably detect up to S bit errors in a codeword, every pair of valid codewords must differ in at least S+1 bit positions, since an error pattern of exactly S flipped bits could otherwise transform one valid codeword into another undetected.

A minimum Hamming distance of only S would allow an S-bit error to land exactly on another valid codeword, which defeats detection, so S+1 is the smallest distance that guarantees every possible error of up to S bits is caught.

## Q5
In CRC coding if the data word is 111111, divisor is 1010 and the remainder is 110. Which of the following code is true?

## Q5 - Options
(A) 011111101
(B) 001010110
(C) 111111110
(D) 110111111

## Q5 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Hamming Code, Error Detection & Bit Stuffing
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (11 Mar, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q36

The CRC transmitted codeword is formed by appending the computed remainder directly onto the end of the original data word, with no other change.

Appending remainder 110 to data word 111111 gives 111111 followed by 110, which is 111111110.

## Q6
The representation of 4 bit code 1101 into 7 bit, even parity Hamming code is

## Q6 - Options
(A) (1010101)
(B) (1111001)
(C) (1011101)
(D) (1110000)

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Hamming Code, Error Detection & Bit Stuffing
**Source:** UGC NET Oct 2022 (8 Oct, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q5

Place data bits 1, 1, 0, 1 at positions 3, 5, 6, 7 and parity bits at positions 1, 2, 4 of a 7-bit codeword.

p1 covers positions 1, 3, 5, 7 (values 1, 1, 1) so p1 must be 1 to keep the group even p2 covers positions 2, 3, 6, 7 (values 1, 0, 1) so p2 must be 0 to keep the group even p4 covers positions 4, 5, 6, 7 (values 1, 0, 1) so p4 must be 0 to keep the group even

Reading positions 1 through 7 gives 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, which is 1010101.

## Q7
Let G(x) be the generator polynomial used for CRC checking. The condition that G(x) must satisfy to catch all errors consisting of an odd number of inverted bits is:

## Q7 - Options
(A) (x + 1) is a factor of G(x)
(B) (x - 1) is a factor of G(x)
(C) (x^2 + 1) is a factor of G(x)
(D) (1 - x^2) is a factor of G(x)

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Hamming Code, Error Detection & Bit Stuffing
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2021 (26 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q100

An error pattern E(x) with an odd number of 1-terms evaluates to 1 at x = 1, so it is not divisible by (x + 1). If (x + 1) divides G(x), then G(x) cannot divide such an E(x), so the CRC remainder is non-zero and every odd-bit error is detected.

## Q8
A code has valid words 0000000000, 0000011111, 1111100000, and 1111111111. If the received word is 0000000111, which word was sent?

## Q8 - Options
(A) 0000011111
(B) 0000000000
(C) 1111100000
(D) 1111111111

## Q8 - Hint
**Answer:** A
**Topic:** Hamming Code, Error Detection & Bit Stuffing
**Source:** UGC NET Nov 2020 (11 Nov, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q31

Decode by minimum Hamming distance. The received word differs from 0000011111 in two positions but from 0000000000 in three positions; the two words beginning with 11111 are farther away.
